title: All in good time — For a world of good
body_markdown:
### All in good time — For a world of good


#### Creating a brand that doesn’t defy all odds but rather embraces them. 👐


Good things indeed take time — a sentiment that perfectly encapsulates how Farmtheory has evolved into the brand we see today. When we first stepped into the Headless Hippies’ *post-it room* , everyone had an individual idea of why we exist, what we dream of becoming, the values, and the people that matter in our journey. Although their ideas were their voices, we asked ourselves, “Is this Farmtheory’s voice as a brand?” We listened closely and realised that we were close but also far.


> We unofficially call it the post-it room, not only for the post-its adorning the four walls but also for how good ideas seem to stick when we’re there.


So, we went back to the proverbial drawing board. We learned from our farmers, caught up with our food business partners, and understood their perspectives on why Farmtheory exists, what it is, and what it should become, as well as the values and people that matter in our journey. But was that Farmtheory’s voice as a brand? We listened closely again and realised that we were now closer (and not that far).


Good things take time, and we soon found Farmtheory’s voice. Everyone now had a common idea of why we exist, what we dream of becoming, the values, and the people that matter in our journey. When people thought of how Farmtheory sounds, talks, looks, and feels, there was one identical image in everyone’s minds. At that moment, if a sketch artist had been called in to paint a picture of Farmtheory after listening to each of our descriptions, the end result would have more or less looked the same. And that’s precisely what the[Headless Hippies](https://headlesshippies.com/) team did thereafter — as sketch artists, they brought our visual identity to life.


Our logo, colours, archetype, and positioning were all textbook elements of our brand that came together, but it was the process that made it beautiful. Google defines a “hippie” as someone who rejects the conventional. With Headless Hippies, we found a partner who, like us, challenged tradition and norms. At every step of the process, we questioned the norm and followed our hearts. We learned to appreciate brands like[Just Eggs.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Rccx_Aa5TE) We understood[what it takes to start a movement.](https://youtu.be/V74AxCqOTvg?si=ZpdCn_1iy10nfZ-H) We bonded over how silly people’s food bias is. We lamented the question that stared at us in the face as we sipped Vibin’s ‘aha’ tea — “All of this is cool, but what alternative term are we going to use for our produce if we’re not calling it ‘ugly’?” In time, as paradoxical as it sounds, the word ‘freeform’ took shape.


Good things take time. And it’s now been more than seven months since anyone at Farmtheory called our produce “ugly.” Without a brand launch, the process had already had a positive impact. Freeform became a way of life, and our brand became real.


With the defensive “ugly” position firmly behind us, we found ourselves questioning — how do we extend this newfound embrace of freeform produce to our tagline? And how do we position Farmtheory as an inclusive brand offering fresh, nutritious produce — both regular and freeform — while creating social impact for our farmers and planet? A tall order to capture in just a few words, but after some time we landed on three that embraced all our produce “perfectly”: **Saving What’s Good.** This elevated us from a defensive position of offering something that is considered inferior, to the vantage position of saving something that is good from going to waste.


But something still felt missing. Yet, good things take time. One fine evening, the Headless Hippies team reached out to us with an insight. At every step of our supply ecosystem, “hands” played an important role — from farmers and pickers to chefs and end-consumers. Hands are used to hold and carry 🤲📦, to save 🪙 🐷👌, to denote what’s good and fresh 👌, to harvest and pick produce 🤌 🫑, to plant a seed 🫰 🌱. A new layer came to life. The use of hands as an element embodied how Farmtheory strives to bring a humane approach to a human-centric industry.


Today, as we launch our brand, we’re celebrating our fruits and vegetables, the silly little food bias that has brought Farmtheory into existence, and the people who help us in saving what’s good. A big thank you to the Headless Hippies team for cooking up a brand with us. Here’s to making a dent in the food supply ecosystem. After all, not all dents are bad? Just ask our brinjals! 🍆
